To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the background action of a sample on signals of the microwave microscope can be reduced by increasing the ratio of the area of the active part of the probe to the area of the inactive part of the probe and by reducing the roughness of the probe surface.

the background signal is a significant factor in microwave microscopy and that its value is proportional to the area of the microprobe inactive part and inversely proportional to the area occupied by the sample in the sensor aperture.

the microwave microscopy signals formation is characterized by the presence of two components: the signal of the local action of the probe on the sample and the background component, which is caused by the action of the probe inoperative part on the sample.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of the use of the microwave microscopy in the estimation of the parameters of the semiconductive materials.
the problem of the background signals' estimation.
the possibility of the background action compensation by means of the special treatment of the measuring information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the background action of a sample is a very important and serious problem in microwave microscopy.
the microwave microscopy is a powerful method of investigation of the semiconductive materials.
the microwave microscopy can be considered as an effective method for the investigation of the semiconductor structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the background action of a sample on the signals in the microwave microscopy is the most significant for the case of the small microprobe inoperative area and the high degree of the macro irregularities in the sensor aperture.
the background action of a sample on the signals in microwave microscopy is a significant limiting particularity.

the microwave microscopy is an effective method of the semiconductor surface investigation, which is capable to give the information not only on the surface conductivity and dielectric constant but also on the surface morphology and roughness.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the signals of the information and of the background action can be distinguished in a number of the cases, including the most common one, when the sample is a homogeneous semiconductor with a single type of carriers and with a constant conductivity.
the background action of a sample on the signals is not always small.
the signals in microwave microscopy can be interpreted as the superposition of the signals of the local and the background actions.
